latest_release.name: CodeAssist 3.45.0
latest_release.body:
**LAYOUT DESIGNER (NEW)**
- A **design editor for Android XML layouts**: open a layout and switch to **Design** to build the screen visually
- A **palette** of widgets, each tile previewing what it adds. Drag one onto the screen to insert it, or long-press a view and drag it into another parent
- **Instant drop feedback**: a ghost shows where the view will land, and the layout animates into its new shape
- A **property strip** with visual editors for the selected view: text, size, gravity, margin, color and more
- Any property, or an attribute you add yourself, can also be edited in a **dialog**, which applies its changes when it closes
- A **color picker** that leads with the current value, with library colors folded away
- A **component tree** and a compact element list for picking views that are hard to tap
- **Full-screen Design view**, and on a phone **Split** shows the layout itself next to the code, not the designer's chrome
- On a phone the selection's actions (duplicate, delete, select parent) live in the property strip; on a wide screen the panels dock beside the canvas
- Zoom and pan settle smoothly, and tapping outside a panel closes it
- The preview draws the **status bar, clock and gesture handle**, like a real screen
- Your own **custom views are compiled on demand**; one that cannot be shown is replaced by a stand-in instead of breaking the preview
- A scroll view that already has its child refuses a second one, as Android does

**LAYOUT PREVIEW SPEED**
- The **first preview** of a Material layout on a phone is about ten times faster (40 s down to 4 s on our test layout)
- An **edit shows up about twice as fast**, and a view added with a new id no longer forces a slow full relink
- Previews render faster and lighter overall, and the designer no longer parses the layout on the UI thread

**CLAUDE LINK (BETA)**
- **Connect Claude to CodeAssist**: Claude can read, edit, build and test the project you have open, from the new **Connections** page in the assistant
- **Claude Code and Claude Desktop** connect to the desktop app with one copied command
- **Claude on the web or on a phone** connects through a private link: turn on the link, sign in, and add it to Claude as a custom connector
- The link is a secret: keep it to yourself, and **reset it** from the same page if it leaks
- Claude is told how to use CodeAssist, and which tools only read and which ones change things
- **Long tasks keep going**: a build or test run that outlasts one request is handed back as a job Claude can check on
- Screenshots and previews reach Claude as **images**
- The status bar shows **when Claude is connected** and when it is working
- This is a beta: tell us what breaks

**AI ASSISTANT**
- The assistant can now **create modules**, **remove** them, make one module **depend on another**, and **reload the project** after a `module.toml` or build script changes. Before, a module it wrote by hand did not appear until the project was reopened
- It can **run your tests** and read the result of each test
- It can add a dependency to a chosen **scope**, and **remove** one
- On Android the assistant **keeps working when the app is not on screen**, with a notification that says what it is doing and a Stop button
- A long model name no longer squeezes the chat header's buttons

**FASTER ANDROID BUILDS**
- A **clean build** of a Material app on a phone: about 106 s down to about 32 s
- **Changing a string or a layout** and running again: about 15 s down to about 5 s
- **Adding a new resource** no longer renumbers the others or rebuilds every library's `R`
- An edited resource no longer re-merges and recompiles every library's resources
- Linking resources against the Android framework is much faster
- Signing a Run build is faster: the keystore is unlocked once, and the old-style signature is skipped where the device does not need it
- Projects **below minSdk 26** now use the prebuilt libraries too when you Run on your own device
